objective: Al terminar cuentas qué estaba pasando en un momento del pasado con el pasado continuo (was / were + -ing).

warmup.prompt_es: 'Te llamé a las nueve, pero no atendiste'. '¿Qué estabas haciendo?'. Para describir acciones en curso en el pasado se usa el pasado continuo.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I called you at nine last night, but you didn't answer.
lines.es: Te llamé a las nueve anoche, pero no atendiste.

lines.speaker: Lucy
lines.text: Sorry, I was having a shower.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: And at ten? I sent you a message.
lines.es: ¿Y a las diez? Te mandé un mensaje.

lines.speaker: Lucy
lines.text: I was talking to my sister on the phone. We were planning a trip.
lines.es: Estaba hablando por teléfono con mi hermana. Estábamos planeando un viaje.

lines.speaker: Lucy
lines.text: No, she wasn't. Her friends were coming too.

explanation.md_es:
**Pasado continuo = was / were + verbo-ing** → acción **en curso** en un momento del pasado.

| | Forma | Ejemplo |
|---|---|---|
| Afirmativa | I / he / she / it **was** · you / we / they **were** + -ing | *I was having a shower.* · *We were planning a trip.* |
| Negativa | **wasn't / weren't** + -ing | *She wasn't travelling alone.* |
| Pregunta | **Was / Were** + sujeto + -ing? | *What were you doing at ten?* |
| Respuesta corta | Yes, I **was**. / No, they **weren't**. | *Was she travelling alone? — No, she wasn't.* |

**Momento concreto:** *at nine last night · at 8 o'clock yesterday · this time last week*. Describes lo que estaba pasando en ese instante.

**Ortografía de -ing:** *have → having · plan → planning · travel → travelling (UK) · sit → sitting*.

**Ojo:** los verbos de estado (*know, like, want*) no se usan en continuo: *I knew the answer* (no *I was knowing*).

Pronunciación: *was* /wɒz/ (débil /wəz/) · *were* /wɜː/ (débil /wə/).
